terminal.description: The home page runs in the Browser panel and reloads every time you save. The shell is here if you want to look around the files.

tasks.title: Link the stylesheet from both pages
tasks.description:
There is a new file next to the pages, `styles.css`, with Dilys's notes in a comment. No page uses it yet.

In the head of `index.html` and of `classes.html`, add a `link` that loads `styles.css` as a stylesheet.

The check reads the head of each page and looks for a link whose address leads to `styles.css` and that says it is a stylesheet.
nextSteps: Read "Where CSS lives" in the lesson.
Open index.html and find the head.
Add the link after the title, save, and do the same in classes.html.
hints: The element that loads a stylesheet has no closing tag and sits in the head.
A `link` needs two attributes: `rel` says what the file is for, `href` says where it is.
In both heads, write `<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css" />`.

tasks.title: Paint the page in the studio's colours
tasks.description:
Dilys wants the cream of the studio walls behind the page and the dark brown of the clay for the writing. Her notes in `styles.css` give both as colour codes.

Write a rule for the `body` that sets its `background-color` and its `color` to her codes. Use the codes, not a colour name.

The check opens the home page with only `styles.css` applied and reads the background colour and the text colour of the body.
nextSteps: Read "A rule" and "Colours" in the lesson.
Under the comment in styles.css, start a rule for the body.
Add one declaration for the background and one for the text, with Dilys's codes.
Save, watch the Browser panel change, and press Check.
hints: A rule names what it styles, then lists its declarations between curly braces.
The background is `background-color` and the text is `color`. Each declaration ends with a semicolon.
The shape is `body { background-color: ...; color: ...; }`, with the two codes from the notes.

tasks.title: Set the studio's letters
tasks.description:
Dilys wants the letters of the sign over the door, Georgia, and writing big enough to read without glasses.

In the same `body` rule, set `font-family` to Georgia with `serif` after it to fall back on, and `font-size` to the size in her notes, written in px.

The check reads the font list and the text size of the body with only `styles.css` applied.
nextSteps: Read "Fonts and sizes" in the lesson.
Go back to the body rule in styles.css.
Add a declaration for the font list and one for the size.
Save, look at the letters in the Browser panel, and press Check.
hints: A font list names the font you want first and a general family last, in case the computer does not have the first.
The fonts are separated by commas. A size is a number with its unit straight after it.
Add `font-family: Georgia, serif;` and `font-size: 18px;` to the body rule.
